leads.title: Gender Recognition Act 2004 of the United Kingdom
leads.documents: Legal status machinery for transgender people in Northern Ireland - provides for official change of gender recognition; requires gender dysphoria and 2 years lived in relevant gender; pre-2020 required applicant be unmarried.
leads.detail: No URL in text; cited as applying to Northern Ireland; introduced after Goodwin v United Kingdom

leads.title: Goodwin v United Kingdom (2002) - European Court of Human Rights
leads.documents: Foundational transgender rights ruling - ECHR ruled UK failure to provide gender recognition violated Articles 8 and 12 ECHR; basis for Gender Recognition Act 2004.
leads.detail: No URL in text; cited as 2002 case, violation of articles 8 and 12 European Convention on Human Rights

leads.title: Sex Discrimination (Gender Reassignment) Regulations (Northern Ireland) 1999
leads.documents: Trans-specific anti-discrimination protection in NI - provides degree of protection for transgender people undergoing gender reassignment in employment and vocational training.
leads.detail: No URL in text; cited by full regulation title and year

leads.title: May 2021 Northern Ireland court judgement on UK gender recognition law
leads.documents: NI-specific transgender legal update - binding ruling that gender dysphoria based on mental dynamic no longer legally required due to WHO 2019 removal of gender identity disorder from mental illness classification; applies to NI only, precedent for rest of UK.
leads.detail: No URL in text; cited as May 2021 judgement by a judge within Northern Ireland challenging near 20-year-old UK law, referencing WHO 2019 decision and DSM-IV

leads.title: Dudgeon v United Kingdom (1981) - European Court of Human Rights
leads.documents: Decriminalisation cornerstone for NI - 22 October 1981, 15-4 majority held criminalisation of male homosexual acts over 21 under Offences Against the Person Act 1861 violated Article 8 right to private life; removed margin of appreciation for morality regulation.
leads.detail: No URL in text; cited with dates: complaint to European Commission 1975, admissible 3 March 1978, Commission report 13 March 1980, referral 18 July 1980, ECHR judgment 22 October 1981; applicant Jeffrey Dudgeon, NIGRA secretary, arrested 21 Jan 1976

leads.title: Northern Ireland Act 1998, section 75 / Good Friday Agreement equality duty - Equality Commission for Northern Ireland
leads.documents: Rights enforcement machinery - statutory duty on NI public authorities to promote equality of opportunity on sexual orientation among other grounds; requires Equality Scheme; Equality Commission monitors compliance.
leads.detail: No URL in text; cited as section 75 Northern Ireland Act 1998 reflecting Good Friday Agreement commitment

leads.title: Employment Equality (Sexual Orientation) Regulations (NI) 2003 and Equality Act (Sexual Orientation) Regulations (NI) 2006
leads.documents: NI anti-discrimination legal status - prohibit discrimination/harassment in employment, higher education, vocational training (in effect 2 Dec 2003) and in goods/services, premises, education, public functions (in effect 1 Jan 2007); notes limited application of British Equality Act 2010 in NI.
leads.detail: No URL in text; cited with commencement dates 2 December 2003 and 1 January 2007; notes DUP motion by Jeffrey Donaldson opposing 2006 regulations failed 39-all

leads.title: Lee v Ashers Baking Company ('gay cake case') - County Court 2015, Court of Appeal, UK Supreme Court 10 Oct 2018, ECHR Jan 2022
leads.documents: Test of NI anti-discrimination enforcement vs religious objection - County Court ordered £500 damages for refusing 'Support Gay Marriage' cake with Bert and Ernie; Court of Appeal upheld; Supreme Court unanimously ruled no sexual-orientation discrimination as objection was to message not person; ECHR dismissed appeal.
leads.detail: No URL in text; cited with County Court 2015 decision, Supreme Court sitting in Belfast from 30 April 2018, unanimous ruling 10 October 2018, ECHR dismissal January 2022; related DUP conscience-clause proposal by Paul Givan 2014

leads.title: Police Service of Northern Ireland homophobic incident data, via Ulster University / Queen's University Belfast researchers
leads.documents: Documented enforcement/safety incidence - reports of homophobic attacks increased yearly from 196 incidents in 2004-2005 to 334 in 2014-2015; researchers note rise may reflect both continuing challenges and growing confidence to report.
leads.detail: No URL in text; cited as Police Service of Northern Ireland statistics 2004-2005 to 2014-2015 with university researcher interpretation

leads.title: Northern Ireland High Court (2012), Court of Appeal (2013), UK Supreme Court (2013) rulings on same-sex adoption ban
leads.documents: LGBTQ family-rights legal status - ruled NI ban on same-sex/unmarried couple adoption discriminatory and breach of human rights; Supreme Court rejected appeal by Health Minister Edwin Poots, aligning NI with rest of UK.
leads.detail: No URL in text; cited as 2012 High Court and 2013 Court of Appeal rulings defended by Department of Health/minister Edwin Poots, Supreme Court rejection 2013
